newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ABARE sees Australian uranium exports rising.
newsitem.headline: ABARE sees Australian uranium exports rising.

text.p: Australia's official commodities forecaster said on Tuesday earnings from Australian uranium exports were expected to grow 23 percent to A$306 million in 1997/98 (July-June) in line with higher production.
The Australian Bureau of Agriculture and Resource Economics (ABARE) forecast production for 1996/97 at 6,000 tonnes rising to 6,800 tonnes in 1997/98.
It estimated total exports of 5,653 tonnes in 1996/97 growing to 6,800 tonnes in 1997/98.
The 1996/97 export figure was 347 tonnes lower than ABARE's March bulletin forecast of 6,000 tonnes.

ABARE lowered its forecast spot uranium price for calendar 1997 to US$13.18 per pound, from the March estimate of about US$17 per pound and decreased its 1998 forecast to US$15 per pound from US$18 per pound.
"Soft market conditions in 1996/97 indicate that inventory levels are high enough to provide fuel security for utilities in the near term," ABARE said.

"However new production capacity is not expected to be available until 1999-2000 and the utilities are expected to take advantage of current low prices to start restocking in the second half of 1997."
ABARE forecast an average Australian contract price of US$15.80 for 1997/98, up from US$15.58 in 1996/97.
NOTE: s - ABARE estimate, f - ABARE forecast
